newsitem.title: USA: Three held in Denver for pipebomb possession.
newsitem.headline: Three held in Denver for pipebomb possession.

text.p: A federal judge Friday ordered three men, including one who was reported to have been in contact with Republic of Texas leader Richard McLaren, held without bond on a charge of illegal possession of a pipebomb and a can of explosive black powder.
One of the defendants, Ronald Cole, has also claimed to be a friend of accused Oklahoma City bomber Timothy McVeigh who is on trial in federal court in Denver.
The FBI in Denver on Thursday raided the suburban Denver home of Cole, 27, and charged him and two roommates with possession of the pipebomb and the explosive powder.

A Federal Bureau of Investigation agent in a court affidavit said a friend of the three recently informed the FBI that the roommates had more than a dozen guns, about 10,000 rounds of ammunition, a mortar, and explosives in their house.

In the affidavit FBI agent Stephen Di Rito said Cole told the informant that Cole heads up a new group, the North American Liberation Army, which has links to domestic and international terrorist groups.
The informant also claimed that Cole threatened to kill anyone who "infiltrated their group for the FBI," the affidavit said.

Cole has said he had ties to the Branch Davidian Cult and blamed the federal government for a botched raid in 1993 on the group's compound in Waco, Texas, where leader David Koresh and about 80 of his followers were killed.

The Washington Post reported earlier this week that Cole talked by telephone Sunday with McLaren, whose group has holed up in a remote west Texas compound and refused orders from police to surrender and face felony charges.

Cole's residence was bobbytrapped to prevent police from entering, the agent quoted the friend as saying. "The roommates have all told (the friend) that they won't hesitate to open fire if confronted by law enforcement officers," the affidavit said.
The FBI identified the other two men as Wallace Kennett, 33, and Kevin Terry, 24.
FBI Spokesman John Kundts said he did not know if Cole had ties to McLaren in Texas.
Cole has appeared at least twice outside the courthouse where McVeigh is on trial.

Paul Graham, who described himself as an acquaintance of Cole and who attended the proceedings, told reporters he believed Cole was "set up" for the arrest. Graham said he and Cole agreed that "now is not that time and place" for militias to have explosives.
Thursday's raid reportedly was a factor in the FBI's decision to step up security for a few hours for prosecutors in the bombing trial.
